content:
alex: ran an overnight perf sweep on qwen2p5 stage pool. noticed ~12% tail latency regression on P95 when kernel-selector v3 routes to autokernel2 (mostly on mixed-lang traffic).

mira: when did this start? any correlation with recent runtime changes?

alex: looks like it started after kernel-selector v3 landed last night (commit abc123). attaching quick flame snapshot from the canary run:
```
samples:
  kernel_selector_decision   48%
  attention_kernel_native    30%
  kv_cache_management        10%
  tokenizer                  5%
  other                      7%
```

sam: is it tied to ropescale heuristics? we flipped ropescale gating for qwen2p5 in the same deploy.

alex: good catch — i pulled timeline. when ropescale=auto and tokenizer produces many subtokens (multilang CJK + emoji), we see more frequent kernel switches and ~2x KV cache evictions per request window. eviction spike correlates with higher tail latencies.

jia: can you paste kv eviction logs? curious if it's index churn or shape mismatch.

alex: snippet from runtime logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:11Z] kv_cache: evict bucket=34 entries=12 reason=batch_boundary
[2026-03-18T02:12:11Z] kernel_router: switched kernel autokernel2 -> native-attn (seq_len_change)
[2026-03-18T02:12:11Z] kvcache: head_kv_dim mismatch detected for model=qwen2p5-v1, falling back to cpu_kv_store
```

mira: head_kv_dim mismatch? we saw a couple of those in canary a while back when loading mixed checkpoints. that's a hard perf hit (CPU path).

sam: tokenizer edgecases often amplify seq_len. CJK sequences -> many subtokens, also emoji sequences. Might trigger ropescale to change behavior mid-request.

alex: exactly. big picture: 1) tokenizer causes burstier tokenization -> longer effective sequence. 2) ropescale/autokernel policy responds causing kernel switch. 3) kernel switch + kv eviction + head_kv mismatch -> CPU fallback. latency stacks.

jia: short-term mitigation idea: add a scheduler priority tweak so kernel_selector favors stable-native kernel when avg_batch_seq_len > 512 OR when multilang_tokenizer flag is set.

alex: tried a quick patch to batching heuristics:
```json
{"kernel_priorities": {"native-attn": 100, "autokernel2": 80}, "heuristics": {"prefer_stable_kernel_if_avg_seq_gt": 512, "multilang_tokenizer_stability": true}}
```
microbench (canary): P50 ~ unchanged, P95 improved from 240ms -> 210ms, cost +0.8% (more native kernels). tail frequency of kv_eviction events down ~60%.

sam: sweet. any accuracy diffs? ropescale changes sometimes slightly affect long-context alignments.

alex: quick eval on our pass/fail set: no functional diffs for generation outputs. but on long-doc retrieval prompts we see a tiny alignment drift when ALiBi+RoPE combo used with ropescale tuned aggressively. flagged for follow-up.

mira: long-term we should: 1) add token-level timing traces (token->kernel routing decision), 2) assert head_dim==kv_dim at model load and fail fast instead of hitting CPU path, 3) refine ropescale hysteresis to avoid mid-request flips.

jia: i'll add a load-time assert for head/kv dims in the loader and emit a metric (model.head_kv_mismatch). Sam can gate canary to fail if metric > 0.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: kernel-selector v3 -> commit abc123 (canary pool: redwood-canary-3)

sam: i'll run a 6-hour canary on dedicated pools with both native-priority patch and the load-time assert. will also add mixed-lang traffic generator.

eng-sre: setting up tracing hooks: token_timing, kernel_switch_count, kv_eviction_count. will alert if P95 regresses >10% or kv_eviction_count spikes.

alex: thanks — leaving a small follow-up patch to force routing to native-attn for qwen variants where head_dim != kv_dim. it's temporary until we can reconcile kv layout in loader.

alex: will post updated perf dump and canary link once sam finishes the run. :thumbsup:
